connections.why: Enterprise is the human input that turns the factors of production into a business
Entrepreneurs write business plans to set out aims and secure finance
Objectives such as growth shape the legal structure a firm chooses
Changing ownership and size alters which stakeholders have influence
Technology like automation reshapes how goods are produced
Global supply chains raise the ethical and environmental questions firms face
Interest rates determine the cost of borrowing to fund a business
The production method chosen affects how quality is assured
Reliable procurement and stock control underpin consistent quality
Research reveals the segments a business can target
The target segment determines how the marketing mix is set
Promotion and product decisions feed directly into the sales process
Fixed and variable costs are the inputs to break-even analysis
Finance choices show up in cash-flow forecasts and accounts
Costs and revenue build the profit-and-loss account
The structure defines the roles a business recruits for
New recruits are inducted and trained for their roles
Development opportunities are themselves a source of motivation
Pricing decisions must respond to economic conditions like inflation
Globalisation lengthens and complicates the supply chain
